title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a working sheet on the genus-1 corner of the Teichmüller tower, i.e. the 'Teichmülleries' programme that later fed into the Esquisse d'un programme. The objects are the once-punctured torus, its elliptic involution, and the four-punctured sphere (pillowcase) obtained as the quotient. My reading is tentative where the handwriting is unclear.

(1) Headline. '𝔖_{1,1} ≃ 𝒯_{1,2} !' records an identification between two objects of type (g,ν), apparently noted with surprise. The left object is (1,1); the right subscript reads (1,2) on the image but might be (0,4). The context points to the classical genus-one coincidence. The elliptic involution identifies M_{1,1} with a quotient of M_{0,4}. Correspondingly, the fundamental group of the once-punctured torus, extended by the involution, is a finite-index subgroup of the orbifold fundamental group of the pillowcase. Equivalently, the Teichmüller groupoid of type (1,1) can be described from the (0,4) data, in Birman–Hilden style. I cannot pin down from the page alone exactly which isomorphism is meant.

(2) Lattice picture. The plane is drawn with the lattice Z^2 (heavy dots) and the half-period points. These are the 2-torsion points of the torus, i.e. the fixed points of z ↦ −z.
- ũ and ṽ are lifts of the horizontal and vertical generators u, v of π_1 of the torus.
- ṽ^{-1}ũṽũ^{-1} is the commutator, the loop around the puncture. For the once-punctured torus, π_1 is free on u, v, and the commutator is the boundary loop.
- ρ̃ is a lifted symmetry, apparently a rotation or reflection drawn with diagonal arrows.
- The matrix (−1 1; 0 1) is an element of GL_2(Z) acting on the lattice. The formula 'ρ(·,1/2) = (1/2,−1/2)' tests its effect on a half-period point.
- r_0, r_1, r_∞ are half-turns (involutions) about the 2-torsion points labelled 0, 1, ∞. These are the images of the branch points of the quotient map to P^1. The identities (ur_0)^{-1} = r_0u^{-1}, (ur_∞)^{-1} = r_∞u^{-1} and (vr_∞)^{-1} = r_∞v^{-1} just use r^2 = 1. Products such as ur_∞ are again half-turns, about other 2-torsion points. So the group generated by u, v and the r's is the extension 1 → Z^2 (or F_2) → G → Z/2 → 1. This is the orbifold fundamental group of the pillowcase, generated by order-two elements whose suitable products give the torus translations.

(3) Bottom of the page: an explicit model of this extended group. Take a group acting on a space or covering, with base point a. An element is a pair (u, l), where u is an automorphism and l is a path from a to u(a). The composition law is (u,l)(u',l') = (uu', u(l')·l), where the path l: a → ua is followed by u(l'): ua → uu'a. The marginal checks l: a→ua, l': a→u'a, u'(l): u'a→u'ua, u(l'): ua→uu'a confirm that the concatenation is well-defined. This is the standard description of π_1 of a homotopy quotient X//G, i.e. the orbifold fundamental group, as pairs (g, path a→ga). Grothendieck uses it to build π_1 of the quotient stack (M_{0,4} or the pillowcase) from the torus and its involution. The next page continues with associativity and inverse checks: (l,ℓ)(l',ℓ')(l'',ℓ'') and inverses (l,ℓ)^{-1}.
errors: Minor: as transcribed, ρ(·,1/2) = (1/2,−1/2) is not the image of (1/2,1/2) under (−1 1; 0 1), which gives (0,1/2). Either the argument is something else (the image shows an unclear first entry) or ρ is a different map. This is a scratch computation, not an error of substance.
The order of composition in u(l')·l (first l, then u(l')) is consistent with the path diagram, so there is no error there.

ideas.what: π_1 of a homotopy/orbifold quotient described as pairs (automorphism u, path a→u(a)) with product (uu', u(l')l)
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group of the homotopy quotient X//G / orbifold fundamental group; groupoid-semidirect-product construction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Armstrong 1960s, R. Brown's groupoid methods; also implicit in Thurston's orbifolds)
ideas.where_published: Related ideas appear in SGA1 exposé on fundamental groups and in Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of Teichmüller groupoids and their action); the explicit formula is not printed there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Once-punctured torus as double cover of the four-punctured sphere via the elliptic involution; half-turns r_0,r_1,r_∞ about 2-torsion points generate the extension of π_1(torus) by Z/2
ideas.modern_name: Pillowcase orbifold; Birman–Hilden correspondence; M_{1,1} vs M_{0,4}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the exceptional low-dimensional modular multiplicities M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} and their role as 'building blocks' of the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Puncture loop as commutator ṽ^{-1}ũṽũ^{-1} of lifted lattice generators
ideas.modern_name: Boundary relation in π_1 of once-punctured torus (free group F_2)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a scratch page of routine classical computations: lattice translations, half-turns about 2-torsion points, and the standard pair description of the orbifold π_1. It supports the well-known genus-one and four-punctured-sphere link that Grothendieck emphasizes in the Esquisse. Nothing appears new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The headline right-hand side may read 𝒯_{1,2}, but the context (elliptic involution, 2-torsion points) suggests possibly 𝒯_{0,4}; it is ambiguous on the image.
Line '(vr_∞)^{-1} [?] = r_∞ v^{-1}': the image shows extra crossed or overwritten symbols (something like '(bc)') between (vr_∞)^{-1} and '='.
'r_1 v^{-1}' appears with a trailing mark, possibly an extra exponent or prime; read as r_1 v^{-1}.
The composition law is best read as (u,l)(u',l') = (uu', u(l')l), with the product of paths l then u(l').
